parole.testo: Borrowed into West Semitic from Akkadian 𒀀𒂵𒈬𒌝 (agammum), from Sumerian 𒀀𒂵𒄠 (agam). Compare Classical Syriac ܐܓܡܐ (ʾaḡmā, “marsh, swamp”) and Arabic أَجَمَة (ʔajama, “jungle, brushwood”).
Coined by Eliezer Ben-Yehuda from Akkadian 𒌑𒊒𒁺𒌑 (urudû, “copper”), itself a borrowing from Sumerian 𒍏 (urudu).

Derived from Akkadian 𒂡 (isinnu, išinnu, “festival, fixed time”), from Sumerian 𒂡 (ezem, ezen /⁠ezem⁠/, “festival”), which is possibly a borrowing from Semitic languages itself (comp. Arabic مَوْسِم (mawsim, “season, festival”)).

parole.significato: a get, a document effecting the divorce of a wife from her husband
parole.testo: Probably from Akkadian 𒁍𒁕 (gídda /⁠giṭṭu⁠/, “document or deed written on parchment”), from Sumerian 𒁍𒁕 (gid₂-da, “length”), from Sumerian 𒁍 (gid₂, “to drag, to draw up a document”). Compare Classical Syriac ܓܛܐ (geṭṭā, “will, testament, document”), in other Aramaic dialects, a narrowed sense of "wri
Borrowed from Akkadian 𒁾 (ṭuppum, “tablet”), itself borrowed from Sumerian 𒁾 (dub, “tablet”), compare Aramaic דַּפָּא (dappā, “page, tablet”).
From Akkadian 𒂍𒃲 (ēkallum), from Sumerian 𒂍𒃲 (e₂-gal /⁠ēgal⁠/). Cognate with Arabic هَيْكَل (haykal) and Aramaic הֵיכְלָא (hēḵəlā).

Derived from Akkadian 𒆠𒉈 (/⁠kuru⁠/, “crucible, kiln, brazier; log, thick reed; short reed mat, collection of reeds”), likely coined from Sumerian 𒄥 (gur, “a bundle”), hence a place of burning bundles of firewood or tinder. Cognate with Aramaic כּוּרָא (kūrā), Classical Syriac ܟܘܪܐ (kūrā), Arabic كُو

parole.significato: A biblical measure of weight equal to 10 ephah.
parole.testo: From Akkadian 𒄥 (/⁠kurru⁠/), from Sumerian 𒄥 (GUR, “a bundle of barley; standard unit of capacity”). Cognate with Aramaic כּוֹרָא (kōrā, “a dry measure”), Classical Syriac ܟܘܪܐ (kōrā, “a dry measure”), Arabic كُرّ (kurr, “a dry measure; payment of six donkeys”).

From Akkadian 𒂵𒆜𒊬 (GA.KASKAL^(SAR), GA.RAŠ^(SAR) /⁠karašu⁠/), from Sumerian 𒂵𒆜𒊬 (GA.KASKAL^(SAR), GA.RAŠ^(SAR) /⁠garaš⁠/). Also Aramaic כרתא / ܟܪܬܐ (karrāṯā), whence Arabic كَرَّاث (karrāṯ), also Maltese kurrat whence Middle Armenian, Armenian քուռաթ (kʻuṙatʻ).

A loanword from Akkadian 𒊩𒆤𒇲 (lilû, lilītu, “demon”), from Sumerian [Term?] (/⁠lil⁠/, “demon”). Associated by folk etymology with לַיְלָה (láylā, “night”), hence transferred to a nocturnal demon and nocturnal bird.
From Akkadian 𒈣𒁻 (malāḫum, “shipman, sailor”), from Sumerian 𒈣𒁻 (ma₂-laḫ₄ /⁠malaḫ⁠/, “shipman, sailor”). Cognate with Arabic مَلَّاح (mallāḥ).
Borrowed from Akkadian 𒇽𒈬 (nuḫatimmu, “cook, chef”), itself from Sumerian 𒇽𒈬 (muḫaldim). Compare Aramaic נַחְתּוֹמָא.

parole.significato: seah, an ancient Hebrew unit equivalent to ⅓ of an ephah.
parole.testo: From Akkadian 𒊺 (še'um, “grain, measure of grain”), from Sumerian 𒊺 (še, “barley, grain”). Compare Aramaic סָאתָא (sāʾṯā). Unrelated to Arabic صَاع (ṣāʕ, “ṣāʿ”), Ge'ez ጽዋዕ (ṣəwaʿ, “cup, chalice”), Aramaic צעא (“bowl”), and Ugaritic 𐎕𐎓 (ṣʿ, “plate, platter”).

Related to Hebrew עֵדֶן (éden, ʿēden, “Eden”), derived from Akkadian 𒂊𒁲𒉡 (edinu, “plain, lowland; wilds, steppes; land naturally irrigated, untouched fertile land”), a loan from Sumerian 𒂔 (eden, “plain, open country”).
Borrowed from Akkadian 𒎎𒁓 (pūrum, literally “stone bowl, lot”) from Sumerian 𒁓 (bur).

parole.significato: chicken, either male or of unspecified gender
parole.testo: From Akkadian 𒁯𒈗𒄷 (tarlugallum, “rooster”), from Sumerian 𒁯𒈗𒄷 (dar-lugal^(mušen) /⁠darlugal⁠/, “rooster”, literally “bird or fowl of the king”).
